body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 62516f35ed85934238bf19d57dc873e88feaf7d4 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- Seven tapers added to the built-in holder library (SK30/SK40/ISO30, HSK-A63/F63/E40/E32), each with ER chucks and Weldon side-lock holders, drawn by the existing conservative laws (full flange cylinder, 45-degree flare, profile stops at the gauge line, Weldon screw allowance) - the safety-floor-relevant outline is the same engine that the BT/CAT/TTS entries already pass.
- Dimensions recorded and sourced: the decision file (docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders.md) gives every number with its source, the two DIN sources agree (3.2 + 15.9 = 19.1), and the HSK rows agree across ISCAR/GDP/Haimer/TAC. The dropped items (ISO20/25, R8, SF32, machine files) are named with reasons, and the ISO30/Ø46-vs-Ø50 flange distinction is recorded.
- Tests in the same shape as the existing suites: pinning tests per taper, point-by-point outline tests, a twin test (ISO30 = SK30), an every-E32 test over all HSK entries, and the existing library-wide laws run over the new entries too. The Weldon picker test is updated (11 tapers), and the app `holder_reference` test covers every entry.
- Clean merge with main (trial merge with origin/main, no conflicts, no ledger resolution needed).

Results (locally, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4240-review` at the merged head, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib`: 202 passed, 0 failed (all holder_library tests, incl. the 9 new din/hsk tests and the updated weldon picker test).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test holder_reference`: 7 passed, 0 failed - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy` runs over the whole library, so every new entry is judged by reference exactly as its drawn copy.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_holder`: 5 passed, 0 failed - `list_holder_library` names every entry and the MCP surface serves the new names.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Step 5 checks:
- No post/toolpath change, so no example catalog runs were owed. The diff touches only the holder library (tools), a decision file, and tests.
- Light lane: not run. Its twins are motion/app toolpath tests, and the diff is the tools holder library only; the author recorded the same reason in the PR body. This is a note, not a blocker (AGENTS.md "The light lane") - a red light run would be the same note.
- No heavy step: the issue is P6, and this is not a P1-below-the-safety-floor PR.

Requested before merge: none.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
- The decision file calls the HSK f1 ring a "collar" (and the TTS entry likewise uses `ring: "collar"` for its no-standoff ring); the code uses `ring: "flange"` for all HSK entries, so the editor's holder row reads "HSK-A63 flange Ø63 × 26 mm". The standard and makers call the outer ring of an HSK holder both "flange" (Haimer) and "collar" (GDP), so either is defensible - but the doc and the code should say the same thing. Also the SK30/SK40 `ring: "flange"` is consistent.
- `holder_library_din.rs` records ISO30 as the SK30 twin; the two `front_face()` calls in the DIN table test assert 19.1 for both — fine. No issue.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
